items.q: Which gas gives a 'squeaky pop' with a lit splint?
items.why: Hydrogen pops; oxygen relights a glowing splint; CO₂ turns limewater milky.

items.q: How does a pure substance melt?
items.misconception: Gradually over a wide range of temperatures.
items.random_wrong: Mixtures melt at a single fixed point, pure substances over a range.
items.why: Pure substances have sharp melting points; impurities lower and broaden them.

items.correct: By how strongly each is attracted to the paper versus the solvent.
items.misconception: Only by colour — colourless substances can't be separated.
items.random_wrong: All spots travel the same distance up the paper.
items.why: Components move different distances (different Rf values); a locating agent can reveal colourless spots.
